case_name: Gorecki v. Hobby Lobby Stores, Inc.
court: U.S. District Court, Central District of California
claim_type: Hobby Lobby's e-commerce website inaccessible to blind screen reader users
outcome: Settled (terms confidential); case terminated October 24, 2017 after court denied motion to dismiss in June 2017

sources.name: Seyfarth Shaw — Plaintiffs score another victory (Hobby Lobby MTD denied June 2017)
BCLP — California federal court denies Hobby Lobby's motion to dismiss

summary_one_line: Court held Hobby Lobby's e-commerce website is a 'public accommodation' under ADA, rejecting due-process and primary jurisdiction defenses; settled within months.
notes: Filed February 13, 2017. Judge denied motion to dismiss June 15, 2017, finding the website (which enables purchases, coupon use, gift cards, and store-location) constitutes a public accommodation. Case terminated October 24, 2017 — consistent with confidential settlement. Court rejected Hobby Lobby's argument that imposing ADA on websites without DOJ regulations violated due process.
